encoder_comparison_subsample.protocol: Identical balanced subsample of ASVspoof 2019 LA for every encoder; same decoder, same SVM back end (StandardScaler + RBF SVC), C selected on dev EER, eval scored once. Subsample figures: NOT comparable with the full-dataset numbers in results/audio_branch/metrics.json.

verdict.interpretation: wavlm-base is 0.60 pp worse than the shipped wav2vec2-base on 1500 held-out clips. One misclassified clip is about 0.07 pp, so a difference below roughly 0.13 pp is within the noise of this subsample and should not be called a win either way.

channel_diagnostic.source: ASVspoof 2019 LA eval, re-encoded through lossy codecs; same clips, same labels, same corpus

verdict.interpretation: Lossy coding alone does NOT materially change the branch, so the DeepfakeTIMIT failure is corpus mismatch (speakers, microphones, recording conditions), not the codec. Codec augmentation would not fix it; more diverse bona fide training data would.

wav2vec2_svm_extra.note: Computed by scripts/eval_audio_metrics.py from cached embeddings and the saved SVM. metrics.json is untouched.

baseline_comparison.protocol: ASVspoof 2019 LA: train fits, dev selects C in (0.1, 1, 10), eval scored once

mfcc_svm.features: MFCC20 + delta + delta-delta, mean and std pooled (120-d)

cross_dataset_celebdf_v2_OLD_MODEL.note: FF++-trained model, evaluated zero-shot (no retraining/fine-tuning) on Celeb-DF-v2. Literature (Khan and Dang-Nguyen, 2023) reports FF++-trained detectors typically fall to 70-75% accuracy on this dataset; compare against that range, not against the 96%+ FF++ in-distribution figure.

heldout_threshold_tuning.source: Dataset source: HELD-OUT self-constructed set: FF++ c23 video drawn ONLY from the test partition of data_splits/split_v2_identity_grouped.json, muxed with ASVspoof 2019 LA eval audio. NOT FakeAVCeleb. Supersedes eval_fallback/ for every claim about the video branch; eval_fallback/ is kept as the in-distribution version.. Never report this as a FakeAVCeleb result unless the manifest's own source field says so.
heldout_threshold_tuning.method: Grid search over |p_video - p_audio| >= T as the disagreement predictor, F1 against ground truth (RVFA/FVRA = should disagree, RVRA/FVFA = should not).

heldout_advantage_bootstrap.caveats: Clips are resampled independently but real videos repeat across RVRA and RVFA, so the interval is slightly narrow. Self-built set, not FakeAVCeleb. Clips without an audio score are excluded.

fallback_advantage_bootstrap.caveats: Clips are resampled independently but real videos repeat across RVRA and RVFA, so the interval is slightly narrow. Self-built set, not FakeAVCeleb. Clips without an audio score are excluded.

shipped_model.video_accuracy_source: cross-validated: pooled out-of-fold clip accuracy over all 400 videos, 5 identity-grouped folds (results/cv/cv5_xcep_mm/cv_summary.json), 95% interval 79.2% to 86.2%. Chosen over the 96.2% figure from the 44-video test split because the PPR's weighting basis (Large, Lines and Bagnall, 2019) is cross-validated accuracy and the small split is optimistic.

video_accuracy_alternatives.note: The figure above in video_accuracy is the one fusion.py uses as the weight; this records what else was available.
